chapters.category: Greek and Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 11 — Heaven's Blessing, Truth, and Peace
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language witness available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic wording has been identified for 1 Enoch 11. The Greek Codex Panopolitanus preserves the complete two-verse unit and is the translation base; the full Ethiopic (Geʽez) textual tradition confirms its position and continuity between the judgment commission of Chapter 10 and Enoch's mission beginning in Chapter 12. No modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: Then I will open the treasuries of blessing that are in heaven and bring them down upon the work and labor of the children of humanity.
verses.study: The voice of the Most High continues the promise of restoration. Human labor, which the giants consumed in Chapter 7, will receive blessing from heaven rather than exploitation. The image of heavenly treasuries presents provision as a gift under God's authority, released for the good of human work.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 28:12 — the LORD opens His good treasury in heaven to bless human work
Psalm 90:17 — God's favor establishes the work of human hands
Malachi 3:10 — heaven's storehouse is opened to pour out blessing

verses.text: Then truth and peace will be joined together through all the days of the age and through every generation of humanity.
verses.study: Restoration is moral and relational as well as material. Truth and peace belong together: peace is not the concealment of wrongdoing, and truth does not end in endless conflict. Their lasting union answers the deception, bloodshed, and lawlessness that filled the earth under the Watchers.
crossReferences: Psalm 85:10–13 — faithfulness and righteousness meet with peace and fruitful blessing
Isaiah 32:16–17 — righteousness produces peace and lasting security
Zechariah 8:19 — the people are commanded to love truth and peace

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 11 is a brief conclusion to the divine answer that began in Chapter 10. After commands to preserve Noah, bind the rebels, end violence, cleanse the earth, and establish righteousness, the Most High promises to open heaven's treasuries of blessing. Judgment clears away what destroys life; blessing supports life and faithful labor.

The reference to human work directly reverses an earlier wound in the narrative. The giants consumed the produce and labor of humanity until people could no longer sustain them. In the restored order, the fruit of work is not swallowed by violent appetite but receives provision from heaven.

Truth and peace form the chapter's final pair. The book does not imagine peace built on ignoring bloodshed or hiding injustice. The cry of the victims was heard, the deeds of the Watchers were exposed, and judgment was announced. Only within that truthful setting can peace endure.

The promise extends through the days of the age and the generations of humanity. This broad horizon links the immediate flood setting with the lasting restoration described at the end of Chapter 10. Chapter 12 will return to Enoch and his commission to address the condemned Watchers.

crossReferences: Deuteronomy 28:12 — heaven's treasury blessing human work
Psalm 85:10–13 — truth, righteousness, peace, and fruitfulness
Psalm 90:17 — the work of human hands established by divine favor
Malachi 3:10 — blessing poured out from heaven
Zechariah 8:19 — truth and peace loved together
